SI-001.q: Social Insurance Law No. 41/2024/QH15 takes effect on:
SI-001.e: The 2024 SI Law was passed on 29/6/2024 and takes effect on 01/7/2025.
SI-001.x:
Basis: Social Insurance Law 41/2024/QH15; Decree 158/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Passed 29/06/2024, effective 01/07/2025, replacing the 2014 Law. Key changes: wider coverage (contracts from 1 month, household business owners, unpaid managers), 15-year minimum for pensions, tighter lump-sum withdrawals.
Distractors: The other dates are wrong.

SI-002.q: Select ALL persons subject to compulsory social insurance under the 2024 SI Law:
o: Employees with labour contracts of 1 month or more
Part-time workers whose monthly salary is at least the minimum SI contribution base
Enterprise managers not receiving a salary
Foreign workers with labour contracts of 12 months or more (except intra-company transferees and those at retirement age)
Individuals on independent service contracts, controlling their own time and methods without management or direction
SI-002.e: Independent service contracts without management/direction are not employment relationships. However, contracts with other names that involve paid work under management are still labour contracts.
SI-002.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Decree 158/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Compulsory participants include (A) employees with contracts of at least 1 month; (B) part-timers earning at least the contribution floor; (C) unpaid enterprise managers; (D) foreign workers with 12-month-plus contracts (except intra-company transferees and those at retirement age).
Distractors: (E) Truly independent service contracts aren't employment. Note: a 'service contract' with pay and management control is still an employment contract (Article 13, 2019 Labour Code).

SI-003.q: Match each contribution with its rate on the contribution salary:
p: Employer – occupational accident and disease fund (normal rate)
SI-003.e: Employers also pay 3% sickness/maternity fund, 3% HI and 1% UI.
SI-003.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Decree 158/2025/ND-CP; Health Insurance Law; Employment Law.
Analysis: Employee: pension–survivorship 8%, health 1.5%, unemployment 1%. Employer: pension–survivorship 14%, sickness–maternity 3%, occupational accident–disease 0.5% (standard), health 3%, unemployment 1%.

SI-004.q: The total compulsory SI, HI and UI rates for the employer and the employee are respectively:
SI-004.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Decree 158/2025/ND-CP.
Working: Employer = 14 + 3 + 0.5 (social 17.5%) + 3 (health) + 1 (unemployment) = 21.5%. Employee = 8 + 1.5 + 1 = 10.5%. Total 32%.
Distractors: B is only the social insurance part; C and D are wrong.

SI-005.q: An employee's contribution salary is VND 20 million/month. How much does the employee contribute monthly to SI, HI and UI (VND)?
SI-005.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Decree 158/2025/ND-CP.
Working: 20,000,000 × 10.5% = 2,100,000 VND (social 1.6 + health 0.3 + unemployment 0.2 million), deductible for PIT (PIT-041).

SI-006.q: With the same contribution salary of VND 20 million/month, how much does the employer pay monthly (including 0.5% OA-OD) (VND)?
SI-006.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Decree 158/2025/ND-CP.
Working: 20,000,000 × 21.5% = 4,300,000 VND. The employer's total cost = 20 + 4.3 = 24.3 million/month (excluding the 2% union fee).

SI-007.q: From 01/7/2026, the maximum monthly salary for compulsory SI and HI contributions is:
o: VND 50.6 million (20 × the reference level of VND 2.53 million)
SI-007.e: The reference level equals the base salary until the base salary is abolished: 20 × 2,530,000 = 50,600,000 VND (46.8 million before 01/7/2026).
SI-007.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Decree 158/2025/ND-CP; Decree 161/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: The social and health insurance cap = 20 × the reference level. From 01/07/2026, the reference (equal to the base salary) is 2.53 million → cap = 50,600,000 VND (previously 20 × 2.34 = 46.8 million).
Distractors: B is the old cap; C is the region I unemployment cap (tied to the regional minimum wage – SI-044); D has no basis.

SI-008.q: August 2026: a department head in Region I has an insurance salary of VND 60 million. What is the employee's total SI, HI and UI contribution for the month (VND)?
SI-008.e: SI + HI on the 50.6 million cap: 9.5% × 50.6 = 4.807 million. UI on 60 million (UI cap 106.2 million): 1% × 60 = 0.6 million. Total 5,407,000 VND.
SI-008.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Employment Law 74/2025/QH15; Decree 161/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Social (8%) + health (1.5%) on the 50.6 million cap: 9.5% × 50.6 = 4.807 million. Unemployment (1%) on 60 million, as the region I cap is 106.2 million: 0.6 million. Total 5.407 million VND.
Note: The caps differ – a common error is applying 50.6 million to unemployment insurance too.

SI-009.q: The salary used for compulsory SI contributions of employees under labour contracts:
o: Must not be lower than the regional minimum wage at the time of contribution
Must not be lower than the base salary
Is set freely by the enterprise
Must not be lower than 50% of take-home pay
SI-009.e: The floor is the regional minimum wage; the cap is 20 times the reference level.
SI-009.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Decree 158/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Contribution salary may not be below the regional minimum wage at the time (floor) or above 20 × the reference level (cap).
Distractors: B – the base salary is for the public sector/reference; C ignores the floor; D has no basis.

SI-010.q: Select ALL items included in the compulsory SI contribution salary:
o: Other additional amounts that are specifically quantified and paid regularly each pay period
Support when an employee's relative marries
SI-010.e: Innovation bonuses, meal allowances and wedding/funeral support are welfare, not SI contribution salary.
SI-010.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Decree 158/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Contribution salary includes (A) job/position pay; (B) salary allowances; (C) fixed-amount supplements paid regularly each pay period.
Distractors: (D) innovation bonuses, (E) meal allowances and (F) family-event support are welfare, not contribution salary.
Note: Inspectors scrutinise fixed monthly 'support' payments – if fixed and regular, contributions are due.

SI-011.q: Under the 2024 SI Law, the 'reference level' is used to compute contributions and some benefits; until the base salary is abolished, it equals the base salary.
SI-011.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Decree 158/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. The 2024 Law replaces 'base salary' with a 'reference level' ahead of pay reform; until the base salary is abolished, the reference equals it (2.53 million from 01/07/2026).

SI-012.q: The deadline for enterprises to pay monthly compulsory SI under the 2024 SI Law is:
o: The last day of the month following the month of contribution
The last day of the contribution month
SI-012.e: For example, October 2026 contributions are due by 30/11/2026. After that, it is late payment.
SI-012.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Decree 158/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Monthly contributions are due by the last day of the following month (e.g., October 2026 → 30/11/2026). Later is late payment at 0.03%/day (SI-014).
Distractors: B confuses it with monthly tax filing; C and D are wrong.

SI-013.q: Enterprises must register employees for compulsory SI within 30 days from the effective date of the labour contract.
SI-013.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Decree 158/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Employers register employees within 30 days of the contract's effective date; late registration may be treated as contribution evasion.

SI-014.q: Enterprises that pay compulsory SI late or evade it must pay 0.03% per day on the late/evaded amount for the number of days late.
SI-014.e: True. They also face administrative penalties and possibly criminal liability if the elements are met.
SI-014.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Decree 158/2025/ND-CP; Criminal Code (Article 216).
Analysis: True. Late or evaded contributions incur 0.03%/day on the amount and days; administrative fines apply, and prosecution (social insurance evasion) is possible when elements are met.

SI-015.q: An enterprise pays VND 300 million of compulsory SI 20 days late. How much must it pay for the delay (VND)?
SI-015.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Decree 158/2025/ND-CP.
Working: 300,000,000 × 0.03% × 20 days = 1,800,000 VND.
Note: Like tax interest, it isn't CIT-deductible.

SI-016.q: Registering a contribution salary below the required level is a form of SI evasion under the 2024 SI Law.
SI-016.e: True. The 2024 SI Law clearly defines late payment and evasion.
SI-016.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: True. The 2024 Law defines evasion to include: not registering or under-registering employees; declaring a contribution salary below the rule; not paying registered amounts… Contributing on the minimum wage while paying far more is a typical risk.

SI-017.q: An employee who does not work and receives no salary for 14 working days or more in a month does not contribute SI for that month.
SI-017.e: True. That period does not count for SI benefits (except maternity leave).
SI-017.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Decree 158/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. With 14 or more working days unworked and unpaid in a month, no contribution is due and the month doesn't count – except maternity leave (still counted – SI-028).

SI-018.q: Statutory SI, HI and UI paid by the enterprise are deductible for CIT; the employee's share is deductible for PIT.
SI-018.e: True. This is where insurance and tax rules meet.
SI-018.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Law 67/2025/QH15; Law 109/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. The employer's statutory contributions are CIT-deductible; the employee's share is deducted for PIT. Unsupported contributions above the statutory amount may be disallowed.

SI-019.q: Match SI contribution period with the maximum annual sickness leave days (normal working conditions):
SI-019.e: Heavy, hazardous or dangerous jobs get more days (40 – 50 – 70).
SI-019.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: Maximum sickness days per year (normal conditions): under 15 years' contributions – 30 days; 15 to under 30 – 40 days; 30 or more – 60 days. Hazardous jobs: 40 – 50 – 70 days.

o: 75% of the SI contribution salary of the month before leave
SI-020.e: The benefit is 75%; certain special cases (long-term illnesses) differ.
SI-020.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: Ordinary sickness benefit = 75% of the contribution salary of the latest month before leave (per working day off). Long-term illnesses have other rates (declining after 180 days).
Distractors: 100% is maternity; 50% and 60% are wrong.

SI-021.q: Female employees giving birth are entitled to maternity leave of:
o: 6 months (for twins or more, 1 extra month for each child from the second)
SI-021.e: Pre-birth leave may not exceed 2 months.
SI-021.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Article 139 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Female employees get 6 months' maternity leave; for multiple births, one extra month per child from the second; up to 2 months may be taken before birth.
Distractors: 4 and 5 months are old rules; 12 months has no basis.

SI-022.q: Match the case of the wife giving birth with the working days of maternity leave for a male employee contributing SI:
p: Caesarean birth or birth under 32 weeks
SI-022.e: For triplets or more, 3 extra working days per additional child.
SI-022.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: Fathers' leave: normal birth 5 days; caesarean or birth under 32 weeks 7 days; twins 10 days; twins by caesarean 14 days; triplets or more add 3 days per child. Taken within 60 days of birth (SI-023).

SI-023.q: Under the 2024 SI Law, male employees may take leave when their wife gives birth within the first 60 days after birth and may split it into several periods.
SI-023.e: True. The 2014 Law allowed only the first 30 days.
SI-023.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: True. The 2024 Law extends the window for fathers' leave from 30 to 60 days after birth and allows it in several parts – more flexibility for families.

SI-024.q: From 01/7/2026, the one-off childbirth allowance per child (2 × the reference level) is (VND):
SI-024.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Decree 161/2026/ND-CP.
Working: One-off childbirth allowance = 2 × the reference level = 2 × 2,530,000 = 5,060,000 VND per child (from 01/07/2026).

SI-025.q: The 2024 SI Law adds a maternity allowance of VND 2 million per child for voluntary SI participants who give birth.
SI-025.e: True. A new policy encouraging voluntary SI.
SI-025.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: True. The 2024 Law adds a maternity benefit for voluntary participants: 2 million VND per child – previously voluntary insurance covered only pensions and survivorship.

o: 100% of the average SI contribution salary of the last 6 months before leave
SI-026.e: Maternity benefit is 100% of the average SI salary of the last 6 months.
SI-026.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: Monthly maternity benefit = 100% of the average contribution salary of the 6 months before leave.
Distractors: B is the sickness rate; C and D are wrong.

SI-027.q: To receive maternity benefits on childbirth, a female employee must have contributed compulsory SI for at least 6 months in the 12 months before giving birth.
SI-027.e: True. If prescribed pregnancy rest is required, 3 months in 12 is enough.
SI-027.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: True. General condition: at least 6 months' contributions in the 12 months before birth. If medically required pregnancy rest was taken: only 3 months in 12.

SI-028.q: During 6 months of maternity leave, neither the enterprise nor the employee contributes SI, yet the period counts as SI contribution time.
SI-028.e: True. The employee still receives an HI card during maternity leave.
SI-028.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: True. During maternity leave (14 or more working days in a month), neither side contributes, yet the period counts as contribution time; health insurance is funded by the social insurance fund.

SI-029.q: A female employee may return to work before the end of 6 months' maternity leave after at least 4 months, with medical confirmation and the employer's consent; she then receives both maternity benefit and salary.
SI-029.e: True. She must notify the employer in advance.
SI-029.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Article 139 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. A woman may return early after at least 4 months with medical confirmation, employer consent and notice; she keeps the maternity benefit and also receives wages for days worked.

SI-030.q: To receive sickness benefits, employees need a certificate of leave entitled to SI or valid documents issued by a medical facility.
SI-030.e: True. These data are increasingly linked electronically with the SI agency.
SI-030.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: True. Sickness claims need a social insurance sick-leave certificate or valid medical documents; data increasingly flows electronically between hospitals and the agency, cutting paper and exposing fake documents.

SI-031.q: Under the 2024 SI Law, the minimum contribution period for a pension at retirement age is:
SI-031.e: The 2024 SI Law reduces the requirement from 20 to 15 years.
SI-031.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: The 2024 Law cuts the minimum contribution period for a pension at retirement age from 20 to 15 years – helping late joiners qualify.
Distractors: 20 years is the old rule; 10 and 25 years are wrong.

SI-032.q: In 2026, the retirement age for employees in normal working conditions is:
o: Men 61 years 3 months; women 56 years 8 months
SI-032.e: Roadmap: men +3 months/year to 62 (in 2028); women +4 months/year to 60 (in 2035).
SI-032.x:
Basis: Article 169 of Labour Code 45/2019/QH14; Decree 135/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: From 2021: men +3 months/year from 60y3m (2021) → 61y6m in 2026; women +4 months/year from 55y4m (2021) → 57 years in 2026.
Distractors: B is pre-2021; C is the end target; D is 2025 for men and wrong for women.

SI-033.q: Match the retirement year with the retirement age for men (normal conditions):
SI-033.e: An increase of 3 months each year from 2021 (60 years 3 months).
SI-033.x:
Basis: Article 169 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Men: 2021 – 60y3m; +3 months a year → 2024: 61; 2025: 61y3m; 2026: 61y6m; 2027: 61y9m; from 2028: 62.

SI-034.q: Under the 2024 SI Law, a woman's monthly pension is:
o: 45% for 15 years of contributions, plus 2% per additional year, up to 75%
SI-034.e: Men: 45% for 20 years; with 15 to under 20 years, 40% for 15 years plus 1% per year.
SI-034.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: Women: 45% for 15 years, +2% per year, capped at 75% (at 30 years). Men: 45% for 20 years, +2% per year; with 15 to under 20 years, 40% for 15 years, +1% per year (SI-036).
Distractors: B is the men's formula; C and D are wrong.

SI-035.q: A woman retires at the normal age with 25 years of contributions. What is her pension rate (%)?
SI-035.x:
Basis: Social Insurance Law 41/2024/QH15 Art. 66 (monthly pension); Labour Code 2019 Art. 169 (retirement age).
Working: Women: the first 15 contribution years = 45%; each extra year +2%: 45% + (25 − 15) × 2% = 45% + 20% = 65%.
Analysis: The cap is 75% – reached by women at 30 years. Pension = 65% × average insured monthly salary (indexed for inflation). Early retirement (where allowed) cuts 2% per year early.
Check: 45 + 10 × 2 = 65 ✓.

SI-036.q: A man retires at the normal age with 18 years of contributions. What is his pension rate under the 2024 SI Law (%)?
SI-036.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Working: Men with 15 to under 20 years: 40% + (18 − 15) × 1% = 43%.
Note: A new mechanism letting men with 15–19 years receive a pension (the old law required 20).

SI-037.q: A man retires at the normal age with 30 years of contributions. What is his pension rate (%)?
SI-037.x:
Basis: Social Insurance Law 41/2024/QH15 Art. 66.
Working: Men: 20 contribution years = 45%; each extra year +2%: 45% + (30 − 20) × 2% = 45% + 20% = 65%. Reaching the 75% cap takes 20 + (75 − 45)/2 = 35 years.
Analysis: Men with 15 to under 20 years get 40% for 15 years plus 1% per year (new under Law 41/2024). With 30 years both sexes get 65%, but women hit the 75% cap 5 years sooner.
Check: 45 + 10 × 2 = 65 ✓.

SI-038.q: The maximum monthly pension rate is 75%.
SI-038.e: True. Women need 30 years and men 35 years of contributions to reach 75%.
SI-038.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: True. The maximum is 75%: women reach it at 30 years (45% + 15 × 2%), men at 35 (45% + 15 × 2%). Years beyond earn a one-off retirement allowance.

SI-039.q: A person who began SI participation from 01/7/2025 may withdraw a lump sum simply because they have not been subject to compulsory SI for 12 months.
SI-039.e: False. The 12-month lump-sum withdrawal applies only to those who participated before 01/7/2025 (with under 20 years); those joining from 01/7/2025 may withdraw only in specific statutory cases.
SI-039.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: False. The 12-month-out lump-sum option applies only to those who joined before 01/07/2025 (under 20 years – SI-040). Those joining from 01/07/2025 may withdraw only in statutory cases (emigration, serious illness, retirement age without 15 years and not continuing…).

SI-040.q: A person who contributed before 01/7/2025, after 12 months not subject to compulsory SI, not in voluntary SI and with under 20 years of contributions, may request a lump-sum benefit.
SI-040.e: True under the transitional provisions of the 2024 SI Law.
SI-040.x:
Basis: Transitional provisions of Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: True. Those who contributed before 01/07/2025, then 12 months outside compulsory coverage without voluntary participation and with under 20 years, may claim a lump sum – protecting rights formed under the old law.

SI-041.q: Under the 2024 SI Law, Vietnamese citizens without a pension or monthly SI benefit receive the social pension allowance from age:
SI-041.e: Lowered from 80 to 75; those aged 70 to under 75 in poor/near-poor households also qualify.
SI-041.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: The social pension for citizens without a pension or monthly benefit starts at 75 (down from 80); those aged 70 to under 75 in poor or near-poor households also qualify.
Distractors: 80 is the old age; C omits the poverty condition; D has no basis.

SI-042.q: Under the 2025 Employment Law, employees on fixed-term contracts must join unemployment insurance when the contract term is:
SI-042.e: The 2025 Employment Law widens coverage from 3-month to 1-month contracts (aligned with SI).
SI-042.x:
Basis: Employment Law 74/2025/QH15; Decree 374/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: The 2025 Employment Law extends unemployment insurance to fixed-term contracts of at least 1 month (previously 3) – aligned with compulsory social insurance.
Distractors: 3 months is the old rule; 12 and 6 months are wrong.

SI-043.q: Current unemployment insurance contribution rates for employees and employers are:
o: 1% each of the UI contribution salary
SI-043.e: The State supports up to 1% from the budget.
SI-043.x:
Basis: Law 74/2025/QH15; Decree 374/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Current unemployment contributions: employee 1%, employer 1% of the insured salary; the State supports up to 1%. (The 2025 Law sets maxima; the Government sets actual rates.)
Distractors: B, C and D have wrong rates.

SI-044.q: The maximum monthly salary for UI contributions is:
SI-044.e: The UI cap is linked to the regional minimum wage, unlike the SI/HI cap (20 × reference level).
SI-044.x:
Basis: Law 74/2025/QH15; Decree 374/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: The unemployment insurance salary cap = 20 × the regional minimum wage – much higher than the social/health cap (20 × the reference level) and varying by region.
Distractors: B is the social/health cap; C and D are wrong.

SI-045.q: In 2026, what is the UI contribution salary cap for employees working in Region I (VND)?
SI-045.x:
Basis: Law 74/2025/QH15; Decree 293/2025/ND-CP (regional minimum wages from 01/01/2026).
Working: Region I in 2026: 5,310,000 VND/month → cap = 20 × 5,310,000 = 106,200,000 VND.

o: 60% of the average UI contribution salary of the last 6 months
SI-046.e: Capped at 5 times the regional minimum wage.
SI-046.x:
Basis: Law 74/2025/QH15; Decree 374/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Monthly unemployment benefit = 60% of the average insured salary of the last 6 months, capped at 5 × the regional minimum wage.
Distractors: B, C and D use wrong formulas.

SI-047.q: An employee in Region I whose last UI month is in 2026. What is the maximum monthly unemployment benefit (VND)?
SI-047.x:
Basis: Employment Law 74/2025/QH15 (unemployment benefit); Decree 293/2025/ND-CP (2026 regional minimum wages).
Working: Monthly benefit = 60% of the average insured salary of the last 6 months, capped at 5× the regional minimum (for employer-set pay regimes): 5 × 5,310,000 = 26,550,000 VND/month (region I).
Analysis: Someone averaging 50 million → 60% = 30 million but receives only 26.55 million (capped). The cap uses the region of the last month's workplace.
Note: Law 74/2025 and Decree 293/2025 follow the question's basis; check current implementing guidance.

SI-048.q: An employee's average UI contribution salary over the last 6 months is VND 12 million. What is the monthly unemployment benefit (VND)?
SI-048.x:
Basis: Law 74/2025/QH15; Decree 374/2025/ND-CP.
Working: 12,000,000 × 60% = 7,200,000 VND/month (below the cap, so paid in full).

SI-049.q: An employee has 48 months of UI contributions. How many months of unemployment benefit are payable?
SI-049.e: 12–36 months: 3 months; each additional 12 months: +1 month → 4 months (max 12).
SI-049.x:
Basis: Law 74/2025/QH15; Decree 374/2025/ND-CP.
Working: 12–36 months of contributions: 3 months' benefit; each further full 12 months: +1. 48 = 36 + 12 → 3 + 1 = 4 months (max 12).

SI-050.q: The contribution condition for unemployment benefits (indefinite contracts or contracts of 12 months or more) is:
o: UI contributions of at least 12 months within the 24 months before termination
SI-050.e: Contracts of 1 to under 12 months: at least 12 months within the 36 months before termination.
SI-050.x:
Basis: Law 74/2025/QH15; Decree 374/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Indefinite or 12-month-plus contracts: 12 months' contributions within the 24 months before termination. Contracts of 1 to under 12 months: 12 months within 36.
Distractors: B, C and D are wrong.

SI-051.q: Under the 2025 Employment Law, unemployment benefits start on the 11th working day after a complete application (previously the 16th).
SI-051.e: True. The waiting time is shortened.
SI-051.x:
Basis: Employment Law 74/2025/QH15; Decree 374/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Benefits now start on the 11th working day after a complete application (previously the 16th) – shortening the wait.

SI-052.q: An enterprise that fails to pay or underpays UI for an employee must pay the employee an amount equivalent to the UI benefits the employee would receive.
SI-052.x:
Basis: Law 74/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. Employers who don't pay or underpay unemployment insurance must pay employees the equivalent benefits they would have received – a direct financial risk beyond fines and interest.

SI-053.q: Select ALL cases in which unemployment benefits are terminated:
o: Refusing twice, without good reason, jobs referred by the employment service centre
Failing to report job-seeking monthly for 3 consecutive months
Starting to receive a monthly pension
Attending vocational training referred by the employment service centre
SI-053.e: Vocational training is a support policy and does not terminate benefits.
SI-053.x:
Basis: Law 74/2025/QH15; Decree 374/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Benefits stop when: (A) two suitable job offers are refused without good reason; (B) no monthly job-search report for 3 consecutive months; (C) a pension starts (plus finding work, military service…).
Distractors: (D) Vocational training arranged by the centre is support and doesn't end benefits.

SI-054.q: Employees receive vocational training support if they have contributed UI for at least 9 months within the 36 months before leaving; support lasts up to 6 months.
SI-054.x:
Basis: Law 74/2025/QH15; Decree 374/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Training support requires 9 months' contributions within the 36 months before leaving; up to 6 months of support at Government-set amounts.

SI-055.q: The 2025 Employment Law allows the Government to reduce UI contributions or provide cash or other support in crises, recessions, natural disasters or epidemics.
SI-055.e: True. This is an emergency response mechanism.
SI-055.x:
Basis: Law 74/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. The 2025 Employment Law lets the Government cut contributions, give cash or other support during crises, recessions, disasters or epidemics – a mechanism tested during Covid-19.

SI-056.q: The HI contribution for employees under labour contracts is:
SI-056.e: Decree 188/2025/ND-CP: HI contribution is 4.5% of the monthly contribution salary.
SI-056.x:
Basis: Decree 188/2025/ND-CP; Circular 09/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Health insurance for contract employees = 4.5% of the insured salary: employer 3%, employee 1.5%.
Distractors: B and C split it wrongly; D has the wrong rate.

SI-057.q: An employee's contribution salary is VND 20 million/month. How much HI does the enterprise pay monthly (VND)?
SI-057.x:
Basis: Decree 188/2025/ND-CP.
Working: Employer's health insurance = 20,000,000 × 3% = 600,000 VND (employee 300,000 VND).

SI-058.q: Electronic SI books and HI cards on the VssID app have the same legal value as paper versions.
SI-058.x:
Basis: Circular 09/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Electronic social insurance books and health cards on VssID are legally equivalent to paper – usable at hospitals and for checking contribution history.

SI-059.q: The maximum monthly salary for HI contributions is 20 times the reference level, the same as the compulsory SI cap.
SI-059.e: True. From 01/7/2026 the cap is VND 50.6 million/month.
SI-059.x:
Basis: Decree 188/2025/ND-CP; Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: True. The health insurance cap = 20 × the reference level, like social insurance: 50.6 million from 01/07/2026 (SI-007) – unlike the unemployment cap tied to regional minimum wages (SI-044).

SI-060.q: A worker's insurance salary is VND 15 million/month. What is the employer's total SI, HI and UI contribution (21.5%) (VND)?
SI-060.x:
Basis: Social Insurance Law 41/2024/QH15; Health Insurance Law; Employment Law 74/2025/QH15 (contribution rates).
Working: Employer 21.5% = social insurance 17.5% (pension–survivorship 14%, sickness–maternity 3%, occupational accident 0.5%) + health 3% + unemployment 1%: 15,000,000 × 21.5% = 3,225,000 VND/month.
Analysis: Employees add 10.5% (8% + 1.5% + 1%) = 1,575,000 VND, withheld from pay; total 32% = 4,800,000 VND. The employer also pays a 2% union fee (outside the 21.5%).
Check: 15,000,000 × (17.5% + 3% + 1%) = 2,625,000 + 450,000 + 150,000 = 3,225,000 ✓.

SI-061.q: A worker in Region II contributes on the 2026 regional minimum wage (VND 4,730,000). What is the employee contribution (10.5%) (VND)?
SI-061.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Decree 293/2025/ND-CP.
Working: The 2026 region II floor = 4,730,000 VND; employee contribution 4,730,000 × 10.5% = 496,650 VND.
Note: Contributing at the floor while paying more is evasion (SI-016).

SI-062.q: A seasonal packing worker hired for the year-end peak on a 2-month labour contract is subject to compulsory SI under the 2024 SI Law.
SI-062.e: True. Labour contracts of 1 month or more are subject to compulsory SI.
SI-062.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: True. The 2024 Law lowers the compulsory threshold to contracts of at least 1 month; a 2-month seasonal contract is covered.

SI-063.q: From 2026, a seasonal worker on a 2-month labour contract is also subject to unemployment insurance.
SI-063.e: True. The 2025 Employment Law extends UI to contracts of 1 month or more.
SI-063.x:
Basis: Law 74/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. From 01/01/2026, unemployment insurance covers contracts of at least 1 month (SI-042), so 2-month seasonal workers participate.

SI-064.q: An employee with a sick child under 3 may take leave to care for the child with sickness benefits for up to how many working days per year (per child)?
SI-064.e: Children aged 3 to under 7: up to 15 working days per year.
SI-064.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: Leave to care for a sick child: under 3 – up to 20 working days/year per child; 3 to under 7 – up to 15 days.
Distractors: 15 days is for ages 3–7; 30 and 10 days are wrong.

SI-065.q: An employee with an SI salary of VND 12 million/month takes 4 working days of sick leave (eligible). What is the sickness benefit (75%; daily rate = monthly / 24) (VND)?
SI-065.x:
Basis: Social Insurance Law 41/2024/QH15 Art. 45 (sickness benefit).
Working: Daily benefit = 12,000,000 × 75% / 24 = 9,000,000 / 24 = 375,000 VND; 4 days = 4 × 375,000 = 1,500,000 VND.
Analysis: The monthly rate is 75% of the insured salary of the month before leave, divided by 24 for a day. Leave counts working days (excluding holidays, Tet and weekly rest). The benefit is paid by the social insurance fund (via the employer) and isn't subject to PIT.
Check: 375,000 × 24 = 9,000,000 = 75% × 12,000,000 ✓.

SI-066.q: Where only the father is eligible under compulsory SI, the father receives the one-off allowance when his wife gives birth.
SI-066.e: True under the maternity provisions of the 2024 SI Law.
SI-066.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: True. If only the father qualifies under compulsory insurance (the mother doesn't participate), he receives the one-off childbirth allowance (2 × the reference level per child – SI-024).

SI-067.q: On termination of a labour contract, the enterprise must coordinate with the SI agency to confirm the employee's SI and UI contribution periods.
SI-067.e: True. This is the basis for unemployment benefits and preserving contribution periods.
SI-067.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Law 74/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. On termination the employer works with the agency to confirm contribution periods – the basis for unemployment benefits and preserved credits; delays can be penalised.

SI-068.q: Enterprises meeting occupational safety and health conditions may apply to contribute to the OA-OD fund at a rate lower than 0.5% (0.3%).
SI-068.e: True. A written request and approval are required.
SI-068.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; 2015 Occupational Safety and Health Law.
Analysis: True. Employers meeting OSH conditions (low accident rates, no penalties…) may apply to pay 0.3% instead of 0.5% to the occupational accident and disease fund, if approved.

SI-069.q: To claim unemployment benefits, an employee must file with the employment service centre within:
SI-069.e: After that deadline, the UI period is preserved for a future claim.
SI-069.x:
Basis: Law 74/2025/QH15.
Analysis: Unemployment claims must be filed within 3 months of termination; if late, no benefit this time but the contribution period is preserved.
Distractors: 1, 6 and 12 months are wrong.

SI-070.q: An employee has 150 unused months of UI contributions. How many months of unemployment benefit are payable?
SI-070.e: 3 months for the first 36; +1 month for each further 12 months; 150 months reaches the 12-month maximum.
SI-070.x:
Basis: Law 74/2025/QH15.
Working: First 36 months → 3 months; remaining 150 − 36 = 114 months → ⌊114/12⌋ = 9 more → 12 months total = the maximum.

SI-071.q: The decree on administrative penalties in labour, social insurance and overseas contract labour, effective 10/9/2026 and replacing Decree 12/2022/ND-CP, is:
SI-071.x:
Basis: Decree 283/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Decree 283/2026 (issued 15/07/2026, effective 10/09/2026) sets penalties for labour, social insurance and overseas workers, replacing Decree 12/2022.
Distractors: Decrees 125/2020 and 310/2025 – tax and invoice penalties; Decree 145/2020 – Labour Code guidance on working conditions.

SI-072.q: Under Decree 283/2026/ND-CP, the fines stated apply to individuals; organisations are fined twice as much (with exceptions), and household businesses are fined as individuals.
SI-072.x:
Basis: Article 7 of Decree 283/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Unlike tax (where decree amounts are for organisations – ADM-059), in labour and social insurance the stated fines are for individuals; organisations pay double; household businesses are treated like individuals.

SI-073.q: Under Decree 283/2026/ND-CP, late payment of compulsory SI (underpaying or not paying the amount due) is fined:
SI-073.e: Article 43(3) of Decree 283/2026/ND-CP; the late amount plus 0.03% per day must also be paid.
o: 12% to 15% of the total amount due, up to VND 75 million (individual level)
SI-073.x:
Basis: Article 43(3) of Decree 283/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Late compulsory contributions are fined 12–15% of the amount due, up to 75 million VND (individual level; organisations double), plus the arrears and 0.03%/day.
Distractors: B is the evasion rate (SI-074); C and D are wrong.

SI-074.q: Under Decree 283/2026/ND-CP, evading compulsory SI by registering a salary below the required level is fined:
SI-074.e: Article 44(2) of Decree 283/2026/ND-CP; evasion fines exceed late-payment fines.
o: 18% to 20% of the evaded amount, up to VND 75 million (individual level)
SI-074.x:
Basis: Article 44(2) of Decree 283/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Evasion (e.g., declaring a lower salary) is fined 18–20% of the evaded amount, up to 75 million (individual level) – heavier than late payment due to deception.
Distractors: B is the late-payment rate; C and D are wrong.

SI-075.q: Under Decree 283/2026/ND-CP, late SI payment of less than VND 400,000 at the time of inspection is subject to a warning.
SI-075.x:
Basis: Article 43(1) of Decree 283/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Late contributions under 400,000 VND at the time of inspection draw only a warning – a de minimis violation.

SI-076.q: A company (organisation) pays SI of VND 200 million late; the authority applies 12% under Decree 283/2026/ND-CP (individual level, below the cap). What is the fine for the organisation (VND million)?
SI-076.e: Individual level 12% × 200 = 24 million; organisations pay double = 48 million VND (organisation cap 150 million).
SI-076.x:
Basis: Decree 283/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Individual level = 12% × 200 = 24 million (below the 75 million cap). Organisations double = 48 million VND (cap 150 million). Plus the 200 million arrears and interest.

SI-077.q: The Region I minimum wage from 01/01/2026 is:
SI-077.e: Decree 293/2025/ND-CP: Region I 5.31 million; II 4.73; III 4.14; IV 3.70 million VND/month.
SI-077.x:
Basis: Decree 293/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Regional minimum wages from 01/01/2026: region I 5,310,000; II 4,730,000; III 4,140,000; IV 3,700,000 VND/month.
Distractors: 4,960,000 is region I before 2026; 4,730,000 is region II; 5,500,000 has no basis.

SI-078.q: A worker in a Region III area contributes SI on the 2026 Region III minimum wage (VND 4,140,000). What is the employer's total contribution (21.5%) (VND)?
SI-078.x:
Basis: Decree 293/2025/ND-CP (2026 regional minimums); Social Insurance Law 41/2024/QH15 (rates).
Working: 4,140,000 × 21.5% = 890,100 VND/month (employer).
Analysis: Insured salary can't be below the regional minimum; contributing exactly at the floor is the legal minimum. Employees add 10.5% = 434,700 VND. Insured pay must include base salary, allowances and determinable supplements – contributing below actual pay is a violation (back-payment risk).
Note: The 2026 region III minimum follows the question's basis; check the original text.

SI-079.q: September 2026: a director in Region I has an insurance salary of VND 70 million. What does the employer pay in total for SI and HI (20.5%) and UI (1%) (VND)?
SI-079.e: SI + HI on the 50.6 million cap: 20.5% × 50.6 = 10.373 million; UI 1% × 70 = 0.7 million (below the 106.2 million cap). Total 11,073,000 VND.
SI-079.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Law 74/2025/QH15; Decree 161/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Social (17.5%) + health (3%) = 20.5% on the 50.6 million cap = 10.373 million. Unemployment 1% on 70 million (below the 106.2 million cap) = 0.7 million. Total 11.073 million VND.

SI-080.q: From 01/7/2026, the base salary is VND 2,530,000/month under Decree 161/2026/ND-CP.
SI-080.e: True. The SI reference level equals the base salary, so the SI/HI cap is VND 50.6 million.
SI-080.x:
Basis: Decree 161/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. The base salary from 01/07/2026 is 2,530,000 VND; the social insurance reference equals it, so the social/health cap = 50.6 million and the childbirth allowance = 5.06 million (SI-024).

SI-081.q: A female employee with an average SI salary of VND 10 million in the 6 months before leave gives birth to one child in September 2026 and takes 6 months. What is the total maternity benefit (6-month leave + one-off allowance) (VND)?
SI-081.e: 6 × 10 million = 60 million; one-off allowance 2 × 2.53 = 5.06 million. Total 65,060,000 VND.
SI-081.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Decree 161/2026/ND-CP.
Working: 6 months' benefit = 6 × 10 = 60 million. One-off allowance = 2 × 2.53 = 5.06 million (birth in September 2026, after 01/07/2026). Total 65.06 million VND.

SI-082.q: A male employee with a 6-month average SI salary of VND 15 million takes 5 working days when his wife gives birth normally to one child. The benefit (100%, daily rate = monthly / 24) is:
SI-082.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Working: Daily = 15,000,000 / 24 = 625,000 VND; 5 days = 3,125,000 VND.
Distractors: B uses 6 days; C uses 4; D has no basis.

SI-083.q: After maternity leave, if her health has not recovered within the first 30 days back at work, a female employee may take convalescence leave.
SI-083.e: True. Maximum convalescence days vary (5–10 days); the daily benefit is 30% of the reference level.
SI-083.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: True. Within the first 30 working days after maternity leave, if not recovered, a woman may take 5–10 days' convalescence depending on the case (single, multiple or caesarean birth); 30% of the reference level per day.

SI-084.q: The daily convalescence benefit after maternity is 30% of the reference level. From 01/7/2026, how much are 5 days of convalescence worth (VND)?
SI-084.x:
Basis: Social Insurance Law 41/2024/QH15 Art. 61 (post-maternity recuperation); Decree 161/2026/ND-CP (reference level from 1 Jul 2026 per the question).
Working: Daily = 30% × 2,530,000 = 759,000 VND; 5 days = 5 × 759,000 = 3,795,000 VND.
Analysis: Law 41/2024 replaces the 'base salary' with a 'reference level' for some benefits. Maximum recuperation days vary (single birth up to 5 days; twins or caesarean up to 7).
Note: Decree 161/2026 and the 2,530,000 figure are 2026 texts beyond my knowledge; the explanation follows the question's basis – verify against the original.

SI-085.q: A woman retires at the normal age with 32 years of SI contributions. Her monthly pension rate is:
SI-085.e: 45% + (32 − 15) × 2% = 79% but capped at 75%; extra years may earn a one-off allowance on retirement.
SI-085.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Working: 45% + (32 − 15) × 2% = 79%, capped at 75%. The two years beyond 30 may earn a one-off retirement allowance.
Distractors: B ignores the cap; C and D miscalculate.

SI-086.q: An employee at retirement age with fewer than 15 years of SI may continue voluntary SI to qualify or choose a monthly allowance under the 2024 SI Law.
SI-086.e: True. The 2024 Law adds the monthly allowance option for those at retirement age who do not yet qualify for a pension.
SI-086.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: True. Those at retirement age with under 15 years may continue voluntary contributions, choose the new monthly allowance under the 2024 Law, or take a lump sum as permitted.

SI-087.q: The 2025 Employment Law (with new unemployment insurance rules) takes effect from:
SI-087.e: Law 74/2025/QH15 takes effect on 01/01/2026; Decree 374/2025/ND-CP guides UI.
SI-087.x:
Basis: Employment Law 74/2025/QH15; Decree 374/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: The 2025 Employment Law took effect on 01/01/2026 (replacing the 2013 Law); Decree 374/2025 guides unemployment insurance.
Distractors: 01/07/2025 is the 2024 Social Insurance Law date; C and D are wrong.

SI-088.q: An employee in Region II has an average UI salary of VND 45 million over the last 6 months. What is the monthly unemployment benefit (VND)?
SI-088.x:
Basis: Law 74/2025/QH15; Decree 293/2025/ND-CP.
Working: 60% × 45 = 27 million > the cap 5 × 4.73 = 23.65 million (region II) → 23,650,000 VND/month.

SI-089.q: An eligible employee has 26 months of UI contributions. How many months of benefit are payable?
SI-089.x:
Basis: Law 74/2025/QH15.
Analysis: 26 months falls within 12–36 months → 3 months of benefit (SI-049).

SI-090.q: Arrange the steps for an employee to receive unemployment benefits:
SI-090.e: Process under the 2025 Employment Law and Decree 374/2025/ND-CP.
o: Terminate the labour contract and obtain confirmation of UI contribution periods
File at the employment service centre within 3 months
Await the decision; benefits start on the 11th working day after a complete application
Receive monthly benefits until expiry or new employment
SI-090.x:
Basis: Law 74/2025/QH15; Decree 374/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: (1) Terminate and obtain contribution confirmation → (2) file at the employment centre within 3 months → (3) benefits from the 11th working day after a complete file → (4) monthly job-search reports → (5) payments until the term ends or work is found.

SI-091.q: Select ALL items NOT included in the compulsory SI contribution salary:
SI-091.e: A fixed position allowance is a salary allowance and must be included.
o: Fuel and phone support not specifically fixed per pay period
Support when an employee's relative dies
SI-091.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Decree 158/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Excluded from contribution salary: (A) performance bonuses; (B) meal allowances; (C) fuel and phone support not tied to the job each pay period; (E) bereavement support.
Distractors: (D) A fixed position allowance is a salary allowance and must be included.

SI-092.q: Registered household business owners are subject to compulsory SI under the 2024 SI Law (on a roadmap set by the Government).
SI-092.e: True. The 2024 SI Law extends compulsory coverage to registered household business owners on a roadmap.
SI-092.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: True. The 2024 Law extends compulsory coverage to registered household business owners on a Government-set roadmap – part of formalising the household sector.

SI-093.q: The total HI contribution (employer and employee) for an employee with a contribution salary of VND 30 million/month is:
SI-093.x:
Basis: Decree 188/2025/ND-CP.
Working: Total health insurance = 30 × 4.5% = 1.35 million VND (employer 900,000; employee 450,000).
Distractors: B is the employer's share; C the employee's; D is wrong.

SI-094.q: Consider these statements on SI in 2026:
SI-094.e: Employees contribute 8% to SI; the 10.5% total includes 1.5% HI and 1% UI.
o: The SI/HI cap from 01/7/2026 is VND 50.6 million.
The Region I UI cap is VND 106.2 million.
Monthly SI is due by the last day of the following month.
SI-094.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Law 74/2025/QH15.
Analysis: (1) True – social/health cap 50.6 million. (2) True – region I unemployment cap 106.2 million. (3) False – employees pay 8% social insurance; 10.5% includes health and unemployment. (4) True – due by the end of the following month.

SI-095.q: An enterprise evades VND 400 million of SI for 60 days. Apart from the fine, how much extra must it pay for evasion (0.03% per day) (VND)?
SI-095.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15; Decree 283/2026/ND-CP.
Working: 400,000,000 × 0.03% × 60 = 7,200,000 VND (besides the 18–20% fine and the evaded amount).

SI-096.q: Employees absent due to self-inflicted injury or drug use are not entitled to sickness benefits.
SI-096.e: True. These are exclusions under the SI Law.
SI-096.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: True. Illness from self-harm, intoxication or drug use is excluded from sickness benefits.

SI-097.q: A man retiring at the normal age with 15 years of SI under the 2024 SI Law receives a pension rate of:
SI-097.e: Men with 15 to under 20 years: 40% for 15 years, +1% per year.
SI-097.x:
Basis: Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: Men with 15 to under 20 years: 40% for 15 years, +1% per year (SI-036). Exactly 15 years → 40%.
Distractors: 45% is for men at 20 years (or women at 15); 35% and 30% are wrong.

SI-098.q: Under Decree 283/2026/ND-CP, multiple unsanctioned late-payment/evasion violations within the limitation period are penalised as one violation with the aggravating factor 'repeated violations'.
SI-098.x:
Basis: Article 7(4) of Decree 283/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Several unpunished late-payment or evasion acts within the limitation period are penalised as one violation with the aggravating factor 'repeated violations' – usually pushing the fine to the top of the band.

SI-099.q: An enterprise's SI payroll for October 2026 is VND 800 million (no one above the cap). What is the total payable by the enterprise and employees to the SI agency (32%) (VND million)?
SI-099.x:
Basis: Social Insurance Law 41/2024/QH15; Health Insurance Law; Employment Law 74/2025/QH15.
Working: Total due = insured payroll × 32% = 800 × 32% = 256 million VND: employer 21.5% = 172 million and employees 10.5% = 84 million (withheld and remitted by the employer).
Analysis: The employer must remit both parts; late payment draws late interest and penalties, even criminal liability (evading social insurance contributions). The 2% union fee (16 million) is paid separately.
Check: 172 + 84 = 256 ✓.

SI-100.q: An employee who unlawfully terminates the labour contract unilaterally is not entitled to unemployment benefits.
SI-100.e: True. This is an exclusion; the UI contribution period is preserved.
SI-100.x:
Basis: Law 74/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. Employees who unlawfully terminate their contracts don't receive unemployment benefits (likewise pensioners and those on monthly incapacity allowances); their contribution period is preserved.
